 **The handoff-deferral makes that rare, and it is the one exception to recording subagents rather than waiting for them (user-ruled 2026-08-27).** The threshold hook holds the reincarnate-seat while any subagent started with the Agent tool is in flight, up to `--ceiling-used-percentage`; at the ceiling it fires whatever is still running, because an agent-session waiting on a subagent that does not finish runs out of context instead of being replaced, which loses more. The 2026-08-23 user-ruling that a reincarnate-seat records its subagents rather than waiting for them (PR [The handoff records the subagents a session spawned](https://github.com/nedsnodes/nedsnodes/pull/153)) governs everything else. The handoff-deferral postpones the kill; it does not do away with it. A subagent still dies at the ceiling, when the agent-session crashes, and on any exit the hook is not there to see.
 
-**The session-handoff is held for a background Bash task too, up to a wall-clock wait (user-ruled 2026-09-14; the wait raised to 75 minutes, user-ruled 2026-09-16).** The handoff-deferral at first saw only subagents. On 2026-09-14 agent-session 831c08ee handed off at 50% while a cold-read-full-run, launched by `nn-systems/cold-read/cold-read-grid.py` as six cold-read-cells (reviewers), ran as a background Bash task; the hook found nothing in flight, the reincarnate-seat killed the grid and its six cold-read-cells 12.7 minutes in, and five of the six reports were lost, because a cold-read-cell writes its report as its last act. The hook now counts a background Bash task as in flight while it is younger than its kind's wait-limit and no completion notification names it, judging each task's wait on its own. A table the hook reads gives each kind its command patterns and its wait-limit, and replaces the hook's `--background-task-wait-minutes` option: the first kind whose pattern matches the command is the task's kind, a command no pattern matches gets 75 minutes, and a kind that only waits, such as `gh pr checks --watch` or a `sleep` loop, has a limit of 0 minutes, so it is never in flight. Past that wait the task is presumed stuck or open-ended and holds nothing, because the transcript carries no process id, the Bash tool does not enforce its `timeout` on a background task, and the task's output file stays empty when the command redirects its own standard output, as the grid's does. The wait was first set to 30 minutes: the user offered 15 as an example, 15 would have killed the cold-read-full-run this was built for, and across 365 finished background tasks on the Mac the 90th percentile was 20 minutes and the 95th 31, with cold-read-full-runs at 8 to 27. Monitors started with the Monitor tool still do not hold the session-handoff: a monitor watches work that runs elsewhere. The ceiling bounds this wait as it bounds the wait for subagents. When a background task other than a waiting-task passes its wait-limit, the session-handoff lists the task's command, its kind, its wait-limit, how long it ran, and the path of the wait-limit table. The next agent-session reruns the task, then looks first for a way to make it faster, such as removing repeated work or running its steps in parallel, and raises its kind's limit in the table only when it finds none.

body: **fix-in-maintenance, nit** Condition: a reader looks up the kind "nc-mutation-testing" this sentence names ("105 for nc-mutation-testing"). Neither the glossary nor the hook's table has it: main renamed the project-term to nn-mutation-testing (glossary line 98), and `BACKGROUND_TASK_WAIT_LIMIT_MINUTES_BY_KIND` in `scripts/handoff-context-threshold-hook.py` names the kind "nn-mutation-testing". The user approved these words before the rename, so changing nc- to nn- is an obvious-error-fix.
